text: The argument from vagueness for universalism (Lewis, Sider) reasons that:
choices: since ordinary objects exist and nihilism denies them, composition sometimes occurs but not always.
since the same parts cannot compose two objects, coincident objects are impossible.
since objects have their parts essentially, composition is fixed and cannot be vague.
since existence and composition cannot be vague and any restricted answer would require a vague or arbitrarily sharp cutoff, composition must be unrestricted.
explanation: The Lewis-Sider argument turns on rejecting ontological vagueness: a restricted answer implies either a vague or an implausibly sharp cutoff to when composition occurs, so if there is no vagueness in what exists, composition must be unrestricted. Distractor 1 is the extensionality/coincidence argument, an entirely different line of reasoning.
